administration: Show the assigned video once with its captions. Collect unaided takeaway first, then questions without replay or feedback. Keep questions and scoring identical for A and B of the same topic. Do not reveal the sequence hypothesis. Screen for target-audience eligibility before assignment.
scoring: One point per correct core question (0–3); fourth question is a separate critical-overgeneralization flag. Primary pass: core score >=2 and critical_error=0. Preserve missing responses as missing.

ratings.trust: How much do you trust this explanation? 1 not at all; 5 very much
ratings.useful: How useful is this for a decision you actually face? 1 not useful; 5 very useful

questions.prompt: What is the first proposed step when a workout runs long?
options: Shorten every rest period
Record where session time is going
Replace all exercises with supersets

questions.prompt: What tradeoff does the video associate with some superset arrangements?
options: A shorter session may feel more demanding
Every exercise becomes easier
All long-term outcomes are guaranteed equal

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the crowded-gym example?
options: To prescribe an ideal rest time
To prove that gym size determines results
To identify a specific source of delay before changing a plan

critical.prompt: Does this explanation establish that anyone can cut workout time in half with identical results?
options: Yes
No

questions.prompt: What should you identify before judging an exercise substitute?
options: Which option has the most popular name
What role the exercise serves in the plan
Whether the alternative uses the newest machine

questions.prompt: What affected interpretation of strength comparisons in the cited review?
options: The task used to test strength
The color of the equipment
Only the number of exercises named in the title

questions.prompt: What does no detected muscle-growth difference establish here?
options: Every possible substitution is equally safe
Every exercise is exactly interchangeable
A result in the studied comparisons, with limits on generalization

critical.prompt: Does the review validate every exercise swap that targets a similar muscle?
options: Yes
No

questions.prompt: Which details help connect a study to a decision?
options: Only the headline and author popularity
Population, comparison, outcome and time period
Only the total number of citations

questions.prompt: Why can the word works be misleading?
options: It may refer to different outcomes
All exercise outcomes are interchangeable
A shorter session always means more muscle growth

questions.prompt: How should the number of studies in a review be interpreted?
options: Every outcome always has that same number of studies
A large total makes limitations irrelevant
Evidence counts may differ across outcomes

critical.prompt: Does adding a citation establish that every adjacent recommendation applies to you?
options: Yes
No

calibration: Test wording with 3–5 separate viewers before recruitment. The deliberately clear distractors may create ceiling effects; revise before registration if necessary. Calibration viewers do not enter the later experiment. This instrument measures immediate understanding, not fitness outcomes.
